title: SEST-1: exhaustive shift testing with streamed linear workspace

claims.statement: For every integer N >= 2 and every secret s in Z/NZ, algorithm SEST-1, fully specified in proof.md sections 2-5, uses n = ceil(log2 N), m = n+1, k = n+2 independent tests per candidate and L = ceil(log2(n+2)); all logarithms are base two. Its total sequential work in the challenge model is T(N,s) = O(N(n+2)(n+1)L^2), including all classical work, addressing, generation, gates, source copies and failures. The uniform bit-length envelope B_T(n) = 2^n(n+2)(n+1)L^2 has growth index exactly 1 as defined in rules.md. The same execution has S_C(N,s) = O(n+1) bits and S_Q(N,s) = O(n+1) qubits. These bounds hold jointly on every execution branch of this one algorithm and configuration, with unconditional full-secret recovery probability > 3/4. All big-O constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes.
